top_strength: The inventory probe was genuinely thorough and well-sequenced — he pulled the existing profile, walked room by room, caught the balcony grill, chased the storage-unit contents down to the six-person table and chairs, and pinned parking distance and stair-carry distance at both ends. He also handled the box-count question well, giving the 15-25 benchmark for a one bedroom when the customer stalled instead of leaving him guessing.
coaching_note: Erik did the work to earn the booking and then never asked for it. He had already told Alexander that September 1 had 'plenty of availability,' and when Alexander said 'I'll share this info with my wife and I'll call back,' Erik's entire response was 'sounds good, I'll email this over.' That is the moment to ask: 'We've got September 1 open — I can hold it for you at no deposit, nothing charged today, and if you and your wife change your mind you just call me.' Compounding it, the wife is going to be shown a price and nothing else, because Erik never gave her a reason to pick Einstein — no No Worries $2,000 coverage, no Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee. On a price-only comparison Einstein loses to whoever quotes lower. Next call: land the three differentiators before the dollar figures, then make an explicit no-deposit booking ask before letting anyone off the phone.
phone_presence_notes: Steady, polite, and consistent with 'perfect / awesome / wonderful' affirmations and natural use of Alex's name, but purely transactional — no humor, no rapport moment, and he audibly yawned mid-call and lost the thread of the customer's answer.
audio_review_reason: Rep yawned mid-call, apologized, and had to ask the customer to repeat himself — worth verifying on audio whether overall vocal energy was low across the call (this was an 18:30 CT call) or whether it was a one-off.
